lines.text: go hand in hand with furtiveness. And when they do dare
to display themselves with cynical frankness, then their
victim is in truth play-acting with a spurious contorted
heroism, and deceives himself at least. But the Christian who
is free with the freedom of waiting for God, finds all such
pretence and mummery repugnant.
"Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons
of God." The peacemakers are those who are always ready
to maintain peace or to lay the foundations of peace; those
who, with their tranquil trust in God, are so inwardly
detached from what they possess or control that they are not
anxiously concerned about their rights, nor do they obsti-
nately insist on their rights. Their inner disposition is so
noble that they are ready to relax their claims; they can
smilingly let slide what to others seems immensely important,
and with a smile and a shrug they can bear to be called
weak.
And finally: "Blessed are those who are persecuted for
righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."
Those who are inwardly detached from the transitory will be
able with their whole power to devote themselves to the
things that are abiding, to the beautiful, the true and the
good, and in so doing they will be without anxiety about any
suffering that may befall them. In the service of the eternal
and the unseen they gladly take upon themselves the burden
of hatred and persecution. Whenever it is a question of God
or the world, they are unhesitating in making a decision
which brings them freedom.
What is promised to the merciful, to the pure in heart, to
the peacemakers, to those who are persecuted for righteous-
ness' sake, is always the same: they shall obtain mercy,
they shall see God, they shall be called the children of God,
the kingdom of heaven is theirs. All this has the same mean-
ing. God prevents them and holds them in His everlasting
love, draws them into fellowship with Himself, and bestows
upon them that which brings fulfilment to their lives.
